    Validation before a release

    Wayu uses several kinds of evidence: tests of the command contract, memory checks, real shell sessions, filesystem/process failures, upgrades and measured startup budgets. A passing run establishes those tested behaviors; it does not prove that every possible input or system failure is safe.

    Automated gates#

    Every push to develop runs the CI workflow. The release workflow calls that same CI and the startup-budget workflow before bumping a version or creating a tag. The gates include:

    • Odin unit tests with leak and invalid-free tracking, strict compiler checks, CLI/integration and golden tests, and TUI behavior tests.
    • Linux AddressSanitizer integration tests and native smoke tests of all four prebuilt targets.
    • A verified previous published binary upgraded to the candidate in Zsh, Bash and Fish on macOS and Linux, including the first shell opened after replacing the executable.
    • Pinned real-upstream compatibility checks and the startup regression budget. Comparative benchmark runs are separate, dated experiments with their own source and machine metadata.
    • A failure campaign covering partial writes, permission denial, interrupted lock waits, hard termination and a genuinely full filesystem on an isolated Linux tmpfs.
    • Twenty repeated fresh sessions for each of Zsh, Bash and Fish on each platform: portable PATH, aliases, Unicode/quoted values, documented variable expansion, file-backend secrets, run-only non-export, periodic rekey/build, turbo export consistency, doctor and private store modes. Homes contain spaces. Fresh source installs and available Bash versions are also tried.

    The failure tests check persisted state and a subsequent healthy write, rather than only an exit code. An ordinary write failure must leave the old store intact. Hard termination may leave the old or new committed entry, but never a partial entry or invalid JSON. Its twenty seeded kill delays do not guarantee interruption at a particular syscall.

    The risk register has 24 scenarios across 12 dimensions. All 16 high/critical cases map to runnable checks; low/medium gaps are explicit. The portable file-size limit produces EFBIG; the Linux full-filesystem case produces ENOSPC. Those are different tests, not interchangeable evidence.

    Reproduce and inspect evidence#

    After building a candidate:

    WAYU_BIN="$PWD/bin/wayu" ruby tests/scenarios/failure_campaign.scenario.test.rb
WAYU_BIN="$PWD/bin/wayu" WAYU_TRIAL_ROUNDS=20 \
WAYU_TRIAL_REPORT=evidence/candidate-trial.json ruby tests/release/candidate_trial.rb

    The portable campaign also runs in the normal and sanitizer integration suites. Real ENOSPC requires the isolated mount prepared by failure-campaign.yml; never point its WAYU_FULL_DISK_ROOT at a normal disk.

    Actions retain unit/integration/TUI logs, source metadata and candidate-campaign-<runner> artifacts. The candidate trial JSON records the binary SHA-256, version, shell executables and round count; it verifies that the original candidate and its trial copy remain unchanged. Artifacts are evidence for their named commit and runner, not a claim about untested builds.

    Observation that automation cannot replace#

    Repeated automated sessions do not constitute multi-day human use. Before a public release, retain a dated daily-driver record with:

    • Candidate commit and binary hash, OS and shell versions.
    • Start/end dates, actual workflows used and any interruptions or recoveries.
    • Problems found, reproductions, fixes and the checks rerun afterward.
    • The maintainer's acceptance decision and any remaining limitations.

    A short automated run cannot honestly fill in elapsed use or human acceptance. Nothing in this campaign publishes a release or promotes the experimental multi-machine secrets protocol. Its independent review remains a separate requirement for removing that experimental status.

    Power-loss/reboot durability, OOM exhaustion, filesystems beyond the tested runners, OS argument-size extremes and ciphertext syncs that preserve an older mtime are not proven by this campaign. The cache and protocol limits are documented in the configuration reference.
